title: Medallion Architecture
summary: A strictly isolated Bronze, Silver, Gold, Consumption and Delivery workspace design on Fabric, with naming standards, reusable load and MERGE code, notebook guidance and Environment setup.
audience: Data engineers, solution architects, platform and security teams

pages.title: Overview
pages.description: What the medallion workspace design solves, when to use it, how the pages fit together and an implementation checklist.

pages.title: Layers and strict isolation
pages.description: The five layers, why each gets its own workspace, the cost of isolation, the options compared and the security controls that apply.

pages.title: Workspace pattern and naming
pages.description: Workspace and item inventory per layer, naming conventions, abbreviations, capacity placement and a promotion summary.

pages.title: Fabric notebooks
pages.description: Notebook capabilities, use cases, sizing and structure guidance, orchestration, monitoring hooks and the verified hard limits.

pages.title: The Environment item
pages.description: Set up one Environment per workspace: Spark properties, resource profiles, libraries, publish modes and workspace defaults.

pages.title: Bronze to Silver
pages.description: Shortcuts into Silver, notebook setup, choosing a load pattern and the reusable full-load function.

pages.title: Incremental loads and MERGE
pages.description: Watermarks and primary keys, the reusable incremental MERGE utility, delete handling and failure modes.

pages.title: Silver to Gold
pages.description: Full loads in Spark SQL and PySpark, plus a config-driven incremental MERGE engine with built-in reconciliation.

pages.title: Consumption and delivery
pages.description: Warehouse load from Gold shortcuts, semantic models and Direct Lake, an AI/ML lakehouse and publishing to the Delivery layer.

pages.title: Appendix: loader internals
pages.description: Generic full-load loaders with filters and transforms, and a line-by-line explanation of the Silver and Gold merge engines.
